paper_title: Optimized Crystal Framework by Asymmetric Core Isomerization in Selenium-Substituted Acceptor for Efficient Binary Organic Solar Cells
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Angew Chem Int Ed - 2023 - Yang - Optimized Crystal Framework by Asymmetric Core Isomerization in Selenium‐Substituted/auto/Angew Chem Int Ed - 2023 - Yang - Optimized Crystal Framework by Asymmetric Core Isomerization in Selenium‐Substituted.md

knowledge_points.content: Three isomeric small molecular acceptors (SMAs) named SCSeF, A-ISeF, and A-OSeF were synthesized by varying the mono-selenium substitution position to central, inner, and outer locations on the central core, respectively.
knowledge_points.evidence: we developed three isomeric SMAs (SCSeF, A-ISeF, and A-OSeF) via subtly manipulating the mono-selenium substituted position (central, inner, or outer) and type of heteroaromatic ring on the central core

knowledge_points.content: The binary organic solar cell based on the donor polymer PM1 and the acceptor A-OSeF achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 18.5%, with a Voc of 0.880 V, a Jsc of 27.2 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 77.3%.
knowledge_points.evidence: Consequently, the A-OSeF-based devices achieve a champion efficiency of 18.5%... along with a higher Voc of 0.880 V... an excellent FF of 77.3%, and a minor larger Jsc of 27.2 mA cm−2

knowledge_points.content: Asymmetric A-OSeF exhibits enhanced molecular planarity and rigidity compared to its isomers due to a unique intramolecular Se...O=C conformational lock, resulting in small D-A dihedral angles of 0.1°/8.3°.
knowledge_points.evidence: A-OSeF with selenium atom at the outermost position of core exhibits... rather smaller D-A dihedral angles (4.3°/8.7° and 0.1°/8.3°) due to the unique and shorter Se...O=C conformational lock, which helps to enhance the molecular conjugated backbone planarity and rigidity.

knowledge_points.content: Moving the mono-selenium substitution from the center to the outer position leads to a gradual decrease in average π–π stacking distances in the crystal, from 3.46 Å (S-CSeF) to 3.45 Å (A-ISeF) and finally 3.42 Å (A-OSeF).
knowledge_points.evidence: With the out-shift of the mono-selenium substitution in the central core, the average π-π stacking spaces gradually decrease from S-CSeF (ca. 3.46 Å) to A-ISeF (ca. 3.45 Å), and then to A-OSeF (ca. 3.42 Å)

knowledge_points.content: A-OSeF forms a 3D interpenetrating network with elliptical orthorhombic frame structures (28.6 Å x 23.3 Å) that are more compact than those of A-ISeF and S-CSeF, providing more efficient charge-transport channels.
knowledge_points.evidence: A-OSeF forms elliptical orthorhombic frame structures with a length of 28.6 Å and a width of 23.3 Å, much smaller than those of A-ISeF (28.7 × 23.8 Å) and S-CSeF (28.8 × 23.8 Å)

knowledge_points.content: The A-OSeF-based device demonstrates a low total energy loss (Eloss) of 0.520 eV, characterized by a non-radiative recombination loss (ΔE3) of 0.203 eV and an electroluminescence external quantum efficiency (EQE_EL) of 2.01 × 10⁻⁴.
knowledge_points.evidence: the A-OSeF-based device delivered the smallest Eloss value of 0.52 eV... The ΔE3 are 0.214, 0.194, and 0.203 eV for S-CSeF-based, A-ISeF-based, and A-OSeF-based OSCs... A-OSeF-based OSCs show larger EQEL values (2.01 × 10−4)

knowledge_points.content: PM1:A-OSeF blend films exhibit an optimized nanofibrous morphology with a proper fibril width of 12.3 nm, which facilitates efficient exciton dissociation and charge transport.
knowledge_points.evidence: PM1:A-OSeF films exhibit more regular fiber-like aggregates with proper fibril widths of 12.3 nm (Figure S15), which is conducive to charge generation and transport.

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis reveals that PM1:A-OSeF blend films maintain a characteristic diffraction peak at 0.46 Å⁻¹ in the in-plane direction, suggesting the existence of pure microdomains that help restrain charge recombination.
knowledge_points.evidence: the characteristic diffraction peak of A-OSeF at ca. 0.46 Å−1 in the IP direction can be maintained in GIWAXS patterns of PM1:A-OSeF films, suggesting the existence of pure microdomain for A-OSeF.

knowledge_points.content: DFT simulations indicate that the asymmetric A-OSeF possesses a significantly larger dipole moment (1.63 Debye) compared to A-ISeF (0.41 Debye) and symmetric S-CSeF (0.24 Debye), facilitating stronger molecular aggregation.
knowledge_points.evidence: resulting in a larger dipole moment of 0.41 Debye for A-ISeF and 1.63 Debye for A-OSeF than that of 0.24 Debye for S-CSeF, which can facilitate the molecular aggregation

knowledge_points.content: Organic solar cells based on the PM1:A-OSeF blend show good thermal stability, retaining over 85% of their initial PCE after 250 hours of aging at 60 °C in a nitrogen atmosphere.
knowledge_points.evidence: the devices based on PM1:S-CSeF, PM1:A-ISeF, and PM1:A-OSeF exhibited over 85% of their initial PCE after 250 h under 60 °C in N2 filled glove box

knowledge_points.content: The A-OSeF-based devices exhibit the highest and most balanced carrier mobilities among the three isomers, with a photo-CELIV mobility of 1.44 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.
knowledge_points.evidence: The μ of A-OSeF-based OSCs is 1.44 × 10−4 cm2 V−1 s−1... The A-OSeF-based OSCs exhibit the highest and most balanced μe and μh values

knowledge_points.content: The exciton dissociation probability (Pdiss) and charge collection efficiency (Pcoll) for the PM1:A-OSeF device are 97.5% and 89.2%, respectively, outperforming the S-CSeF and A-ISeF counterparts.
knowledge_points.evidence: The Pdiss and Pcoll of PM1:A-OSeF devices are 97.5% and 89.2%, respectively, which are much higher than those of PM1:S-CSeF (94.6% and 84.0%) and PM1:AISeF (95.3% and 85.8%) devices.
